title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop affects verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single LLM proposal produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared LLM proposal validated by a deterministic netops verifier and subjected to up to one automated repair iteration if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test was implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01); with n = 1 and n10 = 1 the archived two-sided p = 1.00 under that convention. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; measured marginal verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though the verifier corrected one concrete baseline failure. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being applied to NetOps tasks such as translation of operator intent to device configuration, multi-step change planning, and programmatic repairs. System reports and surveys emphasize that operational safety depends heavily on surrounding engineering: deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback mechanisms [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. An operational pattern widely discussed is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM generates a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks a set of formalized properties, and automated or human-in-the-loop repairs are applied for violations. Practitioners therefore need measurements that isolate the marginal contribution of a verifier and modest automated repair budgets when the model’s proposal is held fixed.

We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment that answers a narrow operational question: given identical initial proposals (shared_initial_candidate semantics), how much does integrating a deterministic verifier and at most one automated repair iteration reduce verifier-detected safety violations compared to the same LLM alone? The design isolates verifier+repair effect (no verifier-guided regeneration) and focuses inference on verifier-scoped properties modeled by a deterministic validator.
sections.related_work:
Deterministic network-configuration verification methods (header-space analysis, route-model verifiers, Batfish-style analyzers) formalize properties such as reachability, isolation, and update atomicity; these methods underpin verifier-in-the-loop architectures in NetOps [Beckett et al., 2017]. Concurrently, multiple recent NetOps/AIOps system reports demonstrate LLMs used for intent parsing and configuration generation while advocating engineering guardrails (e.g., INTA, Confucius, and other agentic NetOps frameworks) that combine models with verification, sandboxing, and rollback mechanisms [INTA, 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026].

Generate–verify–repair has been proposed or instantiated across structured-generation domains to reduce unsafe outputs [PoeTone; INTA], and separate literature documents common LLM failure modes (hallucination, overconfidence, tool-integration errors) motivating verification and human oversight [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. What is less prevalent is a controlled, preregistered ablation that quantifies the marginal verifier effect while keeping the LLM’s initial output identical for both arms. Our work fills that measured, artifact-backed gap by reporting a preregistered paired comparison with full archiveability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory plan. We preregistered study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026 and froze the research question, stratified task-generation seeds, inclusion/exclusion rules, estimands, multiplicity plan, and analysis executor before execution. Primary confirmatory hypothesis: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration will produce a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired within-task). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations.

Task generation and strata. A deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks was created with deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 using preregistered seeds. The preregistered stratification target was VLAN-change = 167, ACL-change = 167, static-route-change = 166; the executed confirmatory set realized those same allocations (VLAN-change: 167; ACL-change: 167; static-route-change: 166) with no confirmatory exclusions (complete_pairs = 500). The generator constrained task payloads to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan} to match the verifier’s modeled scope; full task inputs, seeds, and expected_final_state entries are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl.

Generation semantics, models, and verifier. To isolate verifier+repair effect we used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false): a single shared LLM proposal was produced per task and used both as the baseline output and as the guarded arm’s input. Requested model: gpt-5-mini via hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (provider recorded as openai_responses); configuration details are archived in execution/model_configuration.json (max_output_tokens = 2000, single-attempt generation). The deterministic validator used for gating and scoring is deterministic_netops_validator_v5; its validation rules, modeled property coverage, and the mapping from validator violation codes to severity are included in the archived validator-spec artifacts. The guarded arm invoked at most one automated repair call when the verifier reported a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on the shared candidate.

Primary statistical test and exact implementation. The preregistered confirmatory test is McNemar’s paired test on binary pass/fail outcomes. The archived analysis executor implements the exact two-sided McNemar by forming the number of discordant pairs n = n10 + n01 (where n10 is count of pairs where guarded passes and baseline fails, and n01 the reverse) and computing an exact binomial two-sided p-value for observing n10 successes under X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5). Concretely, for observed discordant counts we calculate p_two-sided = 2 × min{P(X ≤ n10), P(X ≥ n10)} with X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5), capped at 1.0; this implementation and parameters are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence intervals for the absolute difference were computed with B = 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) sampling pairs with replacement.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. The execution completed with model_calls_used = 501 and completed_episode_count = 1000 (500 tasks × shared generation; repair-stage calls observed = 1). Primary counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency table (guarded × baseline): n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Exact McNemar result and CI. Applying the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention yields two-sided p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts (n = 1, n10 = 1). The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729); the analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, the CSVs) and analysis_log.jsonl record these computations and parameters.

Repair activity and discordant episode provenance. Observed repair-stage provider calls = 1 and that single repair produced the sole discordant outcome (the guarded arm converted one baseline-detected violation into a verified pass). The run archive contains the full per-task validator_trace and, when invoked, the repair_provider_trace. For deterministic auditability the repository records exactly one pair where baseline pass==0 and guarded pass==1; auditors can locate the precise pair identifier and its validator/repair traces by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl for that condition. To preserve operational privacy of provider-call contents in the manuscript body, we summarize: the archived validator_trace for the discordant pair reports a preregistered nonzero high/medium-severity violation on the shared initial candidate and the archived automated repair produced a modified configuration that the verifier accepted; raw validator diagnostics and repair-stage provider-call traces are retained in the evidence bundle for deterministic inspection.

Power and ceiling effects. The preregistration targeted power for an assumed baseline error prevalence p_b ≈ 0.30 (N ≈ 384 to detect a 10-percentage-point absolute reduction). Observed baseline failure prevalence (1/500) was far lower, producing a strong ceiling effect that reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements. Consequently, secondary per-violation-class analyses were uninformative due to near-zero counts; these diagnostics and the absence of exclusions are recorded in missingness_summary.csv and deterministic_reconciliation.json.
sections.discussion:
Conditional interpretation. Under the constrained experimental regime — single requested model (gpt-5-mini), shared_initial_candidate semantics, deterministic validator limited to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}, and at most one automated repair iteration — the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals on verifier-scoped properties and the measured marginal pass-rate benefit from adding a verifier+repair was 0.002. This conditional finding documents a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is very high relative to the verifier’s modeled coverage, marginal pass-rate gains from a modest verifier+repair budget may be negligible on a composite pass/fail metric. Nevertheless, the verifier did correct a concrete baseline failure (one archived discordant episode), demonstrating nonzero corrective utility in low-prevalence settings.

Design trade-offs and operational implications. The shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate verifier+repair effect conditional on identical proposals, which answers the operational question faced when regeneration is costly or when policy requires repairing a single human-reviewed candidate. Alternative semantics (verifier-guided regeneration; multiple repair iterations) likely increase final-pass probability at the cost of more model calls and latency; those alternatives were excluded by design and should be evaluated under separate preregistrations. Practitioners should (1) measure baseline proposal error prevalence on representative data before allocating repair budgets, (2) align verifier coverage with operator-critical properties (the verifier-spec in the archive lists modeled properties and severity mapping), and (3) choose generation semantics consistent with cost, latency, and audit priorities.

Statistical and reproducibility notes. The archived exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.00 reflects the executor’s exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small number of discordant pairs; small-n exact p-values can be non-intuitive and should be interpreted alongside effect-size estimates and bootstrap CIs. All artifacts required to reproduce the analysis (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest, model_configuration.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, provider-call traces, validator traces, and analysis CSVs) are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement. The run manifest and deterministic_reconciliation confirm model_calls_used = 501 and observed repair-stage calls = 1.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N = 500) isolating the marginal effect of a deterministic verifier plus one automated repair iteration under shared-initial_candidate semantics. Baseline pass rate was 499/500 and guarded pass rate 500/500 (absolute improvement 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the run’s exact-binomial convention). The conditional finding is: when baseline proposal quality on verifier-scoped properties is very high and verifier coverage is limited, the measurable marginal benefit of a modest verifier+repair budget on a composite pass/fail metric can be negligible, although the verifier retains capacity to correct rare concrete failures. We recommend that operators measure baseline error prevalence, align verifier coverage with operator-critical properties, and select generation/repair semantics that reflect deployment cost/latency trade-offs. The complete preregistration, model prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection of every claim made here.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for entries with baseline scoring indicating a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) and guarded scoring indicating pass == 1; because exactly one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the archived episode and its provider-call traces.
